S100A4 + S100A11 + COTL1 + AIF1: Actin cytoskeletal remodelling enabling phagolysosomal dynamics
PSAP: Lysosomal sphingolipid catabolism supporting membrane trafficking
IFITM3 + SERPINA1: Anti-pathogenic and anti-protease barrier function
suggested_validation: Quantify lysosomal protease activity (CTSS, CTSL) and iron uptake in sorted CD16+ vs CD14+ monocytes using flow cytometry with LysoTracker/DQ-albumin and Calcein-AM quench assays; correlate with feature activation scores via multimodal analysis.

programme_name: Myeloid stress response and lysosomal priming
functional_description: This programme coordinates metabolic reprogramming and lysosomal activation in myeloid cells responding to inflammatory or phagocytic stress. It couples iron sequestration (FTH1), polyamine catabolism (SAT1), NAD+ salvage (NAMPT), and lysosomal hydrolase trafficking (PSAP) with pro-apoptotic priming (BID) and cytoskeletal remodelling, enabling rapid antimicrobial responses while managing oxidative damage and cellular turnover.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron scavenging to limit pathogen access and reduce ROS generation in activated phagocytes
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism produces H2O2 for antimicrobial oxidative burst; coupled to metabolic reallocation
NAMPT: NAD+ salvage maintains energy and SIRT activity during high metabolic demand of immune activation
PSAP: Lysosomal hydrolase maturation and trafficking essential for phagolysosomal killing capacity
BID: Pro-apoptotic licensing balances myeloid expansion with controlled cell death of activated cells
TYROBP/SPI1: Myeloid-specific ITAM signalling and transcriptional control coordinating immune function
STX11/COTL1/AIF1: Cytoskeletal dynamics and vesicular trafficking enabling phagocytosis and granule secretion
CXCL16: Chemokine expression supporting immune cell recruitment and myeloid activation state
suggested_validation: Stimulate CD16+ monocytes and cDC2 cells with IFN-γ + LPS; measure coordinated induction of FTH1, PSAP, and SAT1 by qPCR; confirm lysosomal acidification (LysoTracker) and phagocytic capacity increase together in feature-high vs feature-low sorted cells.

programme_name: Myeloid antimicrobial danger response
functional_description: This programme represents the coordinated expression of antimicrobial effectors and danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) in classical monocytes and myeloid precursors. The dominant S100A family members (A8, A9, A6, A4, A12, A11) form the calprotectin complex and other DAMP molecules that signal infection/danger, coupled with complement activation (FCN1) and actin-binding/inflammatory mediators. This is distinct from general myeloid maturation, representing instead the active priming state characteristic of classical monocytes poised for pathogen encounter.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: Core components of calprotectin (MRP8/14) complex—archetypal monocyte DAMPs released upon activation
FCN1: Ficolin-mediated complement activation—direct innate immune pathology detection
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor central to pattern recognition receptor signaling in myeloid cells
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator induced by IFN—links danger sensing to cytoskeletal responses
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear marker of mature antimicrobially-active monocytes
GRN: Secreted granulins—pro-inflammatory mediators with antimicrobial properties
suggested_validation: Stimulate primary human CD14+ monocytes with bacterial LPS or fungal β-glucans and perform single-cell RNA-seq with parallel protein flow cytometry for S100A8/A9 surface expression; validate that this SAE feature specifically activates in responding vs. resting cells using immunofluorescence co-staining of S100A8 + FCN1 + TYROBP in bone marrow sections.

programme_name: Mitochondrial oxidative metabolism during erythroid proliferation
functional_description: This programme represents the metabolic repriming of early erythroid and megakaryocytic progenitors for rapid proliferation, characterized by upregulation of mitochondrial ATP synthesis, iron homeostasis, and ribosomal biogenesis. The coordinated expression of ATP synthase components (ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1), iron storage (FTH1), and extensive ribosomal proteins reflects the energetic and biosynthetic demands of lineage-committed precursors entering active cell division.
key_evidence: ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1: ATP synthase subunits enabling oxidative phosphorylation for energy-intensive proliferation
FTH1: Iron sequestration essential for haem synthesis and mitochondrial respiration in erythroid cells
RPLP0, RPL37A, RPL4: Coordinated ribosomal protein expression driving translational capacity expansion
HMGB1, YBX1, HNRNPF: Nuclear and RNA-binding proteins supporting transcriptional and post-transcriptional remodelling
NOP10, PA2G4: snoRNP and pre-ribosomal RNA processing required for ribosomal assembly
S100A6: Calcium-binding protein supporting cytoskeletal organisation during mitotic division
suggested_validation: Quantify mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM staining) and oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse) in FACS-sorted pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts vs mature stages; correlate with FAC-sorted population-level ATP synthase protein content by flow cytometry

programme_name: Mitochondrial biogenesis and translational capacity
functional_description: This programme coordinates rapid mitochondrial expansion and protein synthesis machinery assembly in erythroid and megakaryocytic progenitors undergoing intensive proliferation. The simultaneous upregulation of OXPHOS subunits (NDUFB9, MT-CO3), mitochondrial transporters (SLC25A3), ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPLP0), and translational chaperones (PPIA) reflects the bioenergetic and biosynthetic demands of cells rapidly increasing cell mass before terminal differentiation.
key_evidence: NDUFB9, MT-CO3: Complex I and IV OXPHOS subunits essential for ATP generation during proliferative burst
SLC25A3: Mitochondrial phosphate importer required for ATP synthesis and energy charge maintenance
RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPLP0: Ribosomal protein subunits indicating translational machinery expansion for protein synthesis scaling
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase facilitating rapid protein folding during synthesis surge
YBX1, HMGB1: RNA/DNA binding proteins regulating nucleoprotein assembly and mitochondrial transcription
SOD1: Antioxidant defense managing oxidative stress from elevated mitochondrial activity
PTMA, YWHAQ: Signalling and apoptosis-checkpoint proteins stabilizing proliferating progenitors
suggested_validation: Quantify mitochondrial mass (MitoTracker or JC-1) and oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse) in YBX1+/NDUFB9+ vs. negative cells; correlate with ribosomal protein content by immunofluorescence to confirm coupled mitochondrial biogenesis and translation scaling during erythro-megakaryocytic commitment.

programme_name: Nuclear-cytoplasmic reorganization during mitotic progression
functional_description: This programme coordinates the dynamic reorganization of chromatin architecture and RNA processing machinery during active cell cycle progression. The co-expression of HMG-box proteins (HMGB1/2), nucleosomal binding factors (HMGN2), tubulin cytoskeleton components (TUBA1B, TUBB), and hnRNP splicing factors reflects the mechanistic demand to simultaneously compact chromatin, assemble mitotic spindles, and suppress splicing during M-phase entry and mitosis.
key_evidence: HMGB1/HMGB2/HMGN2: Chromatin architectural remodelling required for mitotic chromosome condensation and nucleosome repositioning
TUBA1B/TUBB: Microtubule polymerization and mitotic spindle assembly during prophase/metaphase
HNRNPA1/HNRNPA2B1/HNRNPA3/SRSF3: RNA processing shutdown and mRNA splicing inhibition during mitosis to preserve translation capacity in daughter cells
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic licensing during mitotic checkpoint control and post-mitotic cell survival
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulation (catastrophe/rescue) essential for spindle checkpoint and cytokinesis
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence imaging of Large Pre-B cells synchronized at G2/M phase, staining for phospho-histone H3 (mitotic marker), HMGB1/HMGN2 (chromatin state), α/β-tubulin (spindle), and HNRNPA1 (splicing suppression), with quantification of subcellular localization dynamics across mitotic stages.

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and pre-rRNA processing
functional_description: This feature captures the coordinated upregulation of ribosomal protein synthesis machinery and snoRNP-mediated pre-rRNA processing in early erythroid and megakaryocytic progenitors. The programme is specifically active during the massive ribosome biosynthesis required for rapid hemoglobin or platelet protein production, marked by strong enrichment of ribosomal structural proteins (RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS2, RPS24) and H/ACA snoRNP components (NOP10) essential for 18S/28S rRNA modification.
key_evidence: NOP10: H/ACA snoRNP core component driving pseudouridine modifications in rRNA maturation
RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS2, RPS24: structural ribosomal proteins indicating active 40S/60S assembly
PA2G4: pre-ribosomal RNA-binding protein and growth-associated factor regulating rRNA processing
SLBP: histone mRNA stem-loop binding protein supporting S-phase histone synthesis coupled to DNA replication during progenitor expansion
HMGB1, YBX1: nucleic acid chaperones facilitating rRNA folding and ribosome assembly
suggested_validation: Perform single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) for pre-rRNA intermediates (ITS1/ITS2) combined with immunofluorescence for NOP10 and ribosomal proteins in sorted Pro-Erythroblasts and Megakaryocyte Precursors to confirm concurrent rRNA processing and ribosome assembly.

programme_name: Mitochondrial oxidative metabolism priming
functional_description: This programme represents metabolic preparation for high-energy demand states through coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial respiration, glycolytic bypass, and antioxidant defences. The co-expression of COX5A (oxidative phosphorylation), LDHA (anaerobic glycolysis), and GSTP1 (glutathione detoxification) suggests cells are simultaneously preparing oxidative and glycolytic capacity while buffering ROS. This metabolic dualism is characteristic of megakaryocyte precursors and cDC precursors preparing for rapid proliferation and inflammatory activation.
key_evidence: COX5A: terminal oxidative phosphorylation enzyme—directly indicates mitochondrial respiration scaling
LDHA: lactate dehydrogenase—glycolytic backup during metabolic stress or proliferation bursts
GSTP1: phase II detoxification—ROS scavenging to protect against oxidative damage during bioenergetic upregulation
VDAC1: outer mitochondrial membrane transporter—ATP/metabolite flux regulation
PPA1: inorganic pyrophosphatase—removal of pyrophosphate to drive biosynthetic condensation reactions
ATG3: autophagy machinery—metabolic quality control and lipid catabolism during transition states
ENO1: glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting functions—both metabolic and transcriptional priming
suggested_validation: Measure oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) in feature-high vs feature-low megakaryocyte precursors and cDC precursors using Seahorse XF; validate ROS levels via DCFDA flow cytometry to confirm antioxidant buffering; correlate feature activation with mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM) staining.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte precursor mitotic spindle organization
functional_description: This feature represents a coordinated programme supporting active mitosis and cell cycle progression in megakaryocyte precursors, characterized by upregulation of RNA-binding proteins controlling splicing dynamics, mitotic checkpoint factors, and mitochondrial-cytoplasmic energy coupling. The enrichment of nucleolar and spindle-associated proteins (ERH, DEK, HMGN2) alongside glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, ENO1) indicates metabolic reprogramming to support rapid chromosome segregation and cytokinesis.
key_evidence: ERH: Mitosis factor directly involved in spindle assembly and cytokinesis timing
DEK: DNA topology regulator facilitating chromatin condensation during M-phase
HMGN2: Nucleosomal remodelling protein supporting transcription of mitotic genes
VDAC1: Mitochondrial outer membrane channel providing ATP-dependent energy for spindle dynamics
SRSF3: SR-family splicing regulator controlling mitotic checkpoint kinase isoform selection
YWHAQ/YWHAE: 14-3-3 adaptors mediating phospho-dependent signalling of CDK1 substrates during mitosis
RANBP1: RanGTP gradient establishment essential for spindle pole organization and nuclear envelope reformation
suggested_validation: Immunofluorescence co-staining for phospho-histone H3 (mitotic marker) with ERH and DEK in primary megakaryocyte precursors, combined with live-cell imaging of FUCCI cell cycle reporter to confirm this programme activates specifically during S/G2/M phases

programme_name: Pre-B cell receptor signaling and surrogate light chain
functional_description: This programme represents the pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) complex assembly and early signal transduction, characterized by expression of surrogate light chain components (VPREB3), BCR signaling adaptor (CD79B), and DNA repair machinery active during V(D)J recombination. The erythroblast contamination likely reflects co-activation of metabolic programmes rather than true multi-lineage expression, while TCL1A and CD24 indicate early B-cell developmental checkpoint control.
key_evidence: CD79B: core component of pre-BCR signaling complex essential for allelic exclusion checkpoint
VPREB3: surrogate light chain protein specifically expressed during pre-B stage before true Ig-lambda rearrangement
TCL1A: AKT coactivator regulating pre-BCR survival signals and G0→G1 transition
IGHM: mu heavy chain expression marks transition from pro-B to pre-B developmental stage
CD24: surface marker and negative feedback regulator of pre-BCR signaling intensity
NEIL1: base excision repair enzyme supporting V(D)J recombination fidelity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry gating on CD79B+VPREB3+CD24+ cells combined with phospho-flow analysis of downstream BCR signaling (pCD79B, pSYK, pLyn) to confirm pre-BCR complex activation specifically in this feature-high population

programme_name: Mitotic spindle assembly and proteostasis
functional_description: This programme coordinates microtubule dynamics and proteasomal protein quality control during active cell division. The co-activation of spindle regulators (STMN1, actin-binding proteins), RNA splicing machinery (SNRPG, LSM5), and proteasome subunits (PSMA4, PSMA5) reflects the coupled demand for cytoskeletal remodelling and selective protein degradation in proliferating cells navigating the G2/M checkpoint.
key_evidence: STMN1: Microtubule-destabilizing protein essential for spindle dynamics and chromosome segregation
PSMA4/PSMA5: 20S proteasome core subunits required for degradation of cell-cycle regulators and damaged proteins during mitosis
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein enabling rapid cytoskeletal remodelling for cleavage furrow formation
SNRPG/LSM5: spliceosome components supporting cell-cycle-regulated splicing of mitotic genes
CALM3: Calcium signalling mediator coordinating calmodulin-dependent kinase activity in mitotic spindle assembly
HMGN2: Chromatin remodeller supporting dynamic transcription of cell-cycle and metabolic genes
suggested_validation: Live-cell time-lapse microscopy with spindle imaging (SiR-tubulin) combined with proteasome activity reporter (DQ-ubiquitin) in cells with high vs. low feature activation, stratified by cell-cycle phase using FUCCI markers.

programme_name: G2/M mitotic spindle assembly and chromosome segregation
functional_description: This programme coordinates the active preparation and execution of mitosis through concurrent upregulation of microtubule dynamics (STMN1, TUBA1B, TUBB), spindle apparatus assembly (NUSAP1, AURKB), DNA topology management during replication/segregation (TOP2A), and chromatin remodeling (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2). The co-expression pattern indicates cells in G2/M phase actively assembling the mitotic spindle and preparing for chromosome segregation, distinct from earlier S-phase DNA synthesis.
key_evidence: STMN1, TUBA1B, TUBB: core microtubule components and dynamics regulators essential for spindle fibre formation
NUSAP1, AURKB: spindle pole and kinetochore-associated proteins; AURKB specifically marks the chromosomal passenger complex driving cytokinesis
TOP2A: DNA topoisomerase II critical for unlinking newly replicated DNA and resolving topological tension during mitosis
HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2: chromatin architectural proteins reorganizing nucleosomal structure during mitotic chromosome condensation
RPS24, CALM2, UBB: housekeeping translation and signalling machinery supporting the high protein synthesis demand of mitotic apparatus assembly
suggested_validation: Live-cell imaging with FUCCI (fluorescent ubiquitination-based cell cycle indicator) reporter combined with immunofluorescence for phospho-histone H3 and AURKB localization to confirm cells expressing this feature are specifically in G2/M phase with active spindle assembly.

programme_name: Active chromatin remodeling & nucleosome dynamics
functional_description: This feature captures coordinated upregulation of nucleosome-binding proteins (HMGN2, HMGB2, H2AFZ, H2AFY, DEK) alongside ribosomal proteins and cell-cycle regulators in rapidly dividing erythroid and myeloid progenitors. The programme reflects simultaneous chromatin accessibility remodeling, active translation machinery engagement, and ribonucleotide biosynthesis (TALDO1) required for peak proliferation during erythroid and pre-DC differentiation.
key_evidence: HMGN2, HMGB2, DEK: sequence-specific and non-specific DNA binding proteins that promote nucleosome dynamics and transcriptional accessibility in active chromatin regions
H2AFZ, H2AFY: histone variants enriched at active promoters and regulatory regions; H2AFZ specifically marks dynamic chromatin during S phase
CKS1B: CDK regulatory subunit essential for G1/S and G2/M checkpoint progression; direct marker of active cell-cycle commitment
TUBA1B, TUBB, RPS24: structural components of mitotic spindle and ribosomes; indicate simultaneous mitotic spindle assembly and elevated protein synthesis
TALDO1: nonoxidative PPP enzyme; supplies ribose-5-phosphate for nucleotide synthesis, coupling anabolic demand to proliferation rate
suggested_validation: ChIP-seq for H2AFZ and HMGN2 in sorted polychromatic erythroblasts vs. basophilic erythroblasts to confirm nucleosome remodeling activity peaks at maximal proliferation; correlate feature activation with S/G2M phase markers (e.g., PCNA, cyclin B1) by flow cytometry on high-activation cells.

programme_name: B cell receptor assembly and maturation
functional_description: This programme represents early B cell lineage commitment and BCR complex maturation, characterized by upregulation of B cell-specific signaling components (CD79B, FCRLA) and genes supporting receptor assembly and trafficking. The enrichment reflects a developmental checkpoint where pre-B and immature B cells establish functional antigen recognition capacity through coordinated expression of immunoglobulin-associated molecules and vesicular transport machinery.
key_evidence: CD79B: core component of B cell antigen receptor complex required for BCR signaling initiation
FCRLA: Fc receptor homologue involved in B cell maturation and antibody-mediated feedback regulation
BCL7A: BAF chromatin complex component; dysregulated in B cell malignancies, marks active B lineage differentiation
SYNGR1: synaptic vesicle protein; suggests active vesicular trafficking during BCR transport and cell surface presentation
EPCAM: marks epithelial-like B cell progenitors and immature B cells in developmental transition
ATP5IF1: mitochondrial ATP regulation supports energetic demands of active protein synthesis during BCR assembly
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of Small Pre-B and Immature B cells for CD79B, FCRLA, and intracellular BCR-μ protein levels in feature-high vs feature-low populations; validate SYNGR1 localization to ER/Golgi during BCR trafficking using immunofluorescence or cell fractionation.

programme_name: Stromal complement and haemostasis regulation
functional_description: This programme represents a specific stromal niche function centred on regulating coagulation cascade initiation and complement activation through secretion of pathway inhibitors and modulators. The coordinated expression of complement regulators (SERPING1, CFD), coagulation inhibitors (TFPI), and antiviral interferon-response proteins suggests stromal cells actively maintain a controlled inflammatory microenvironment while protecting against pathogenic threat.
key_evidence: TFPI: direct inhibitor of tissue factor pathway initiation—prevents excessive thrombin generation in niche
SERPING1: C1-esterase inhibitor—master regulator of complement cascade preventing uncontrolled activation
CFD: complement factor D—rate-limiting enzyme of alternative pathway, positioned for direct stromal control
CXCL12: HSC retention chemokine—anchors target cell population to this protective niche compartment
IFITM3: interferon-induced antiviral protein—suggests antiviral surveillance role in addition to coagulation control
GAS6: TAM-ligand growth factor—enhances efferocytosis and dampens inflammatory signalling
suggested_validation: Co-culture of sorted stromal cells with megakaryocytes/precursors measuring thrombin generation (CAT assay) and complement C5a production in media from feature-high vs feature-low stromal subsets; CRISPR knockdown of TFPI or SERPING1 in feature-positive stromals to assess rescue of coagulation abnormalities in co-culture

programme_name: Ribosomal biogenesis and translational capacity
functional_description: This feature captures a coordinated programme of ribosomal protein synthesis and translation machinery assembly, specifically active in large pre-B cells preparing for or undergoing rapid protein synthesis. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins (RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4, etc.) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) indicates active ribosome biogenesis to support the immunoglobulin heavy and light chain synthesis required during pre-B cell development.
key_evidence: RPS17, RPS2, RPS24, RPS23: 40S ribosomal subunit components essential for ribosome assembly and translation initiation capacity
RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins required for peptide bond formation and elongation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor enabling efficient delivery of aminoacyl-tRNAs; directly supports high-throughput protein synthesis
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme supporting ATP/GTP provision for ribosome biogenesis and translation
HNRNPA1, YBX1: RNA-binding proteins regulating mRNA stability and translational efficiency during expansion phase
suggested_validation: Polysome profiling (sucrose gradient fractionation) of sorted large pre-B cells with high feature activation vs. low activation to quantify actively translating ribosomes and ribosomal content; correlate polysome complexity with feature expression level.

programme_name: Nucleosome remodeling and glycolytic priming
functional_description: This feature captures a coordinated chromatin accessibility and metabolic programme active during megakaryocyte precursor proliferation. The programme couples nucleosome-level chromatin reorganization (HMGN2, HMGB1, DEK, H2AFY) with rapid glycolytic metabolism (GAPDH, ENO1, LDHA) to support high transcriptional activity and biomass accumulation during megakaryocyte amplification prior to polyploidization.
key_evidence: HMGN2: Nucleosomal DNA binding protein marking transcriptionally permissive chromatin state required for rapid gene expression during proliferation
DEK: DNA-binding protein inducing positive supercoiling and chromatin condensation, actively remodeling chromatin topology in dividing cells
HMGB1: HMGB-family DNA-binding factor facilitating nucleosome disassembly and chromatin accessibility during transcriptional activation
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme supporting ATP and biosynthetic precursor production for rapid cell division in megakaryocyte precursors
ENO1: Glycolytic enzyme enabling lactate-based metabolism characteristic of proliferating cells with high biosynthetic demand
PTMA: Nuclear protein with anti-apoptotic function, stabilizing proliferating precursor state during megakaryocyte expansion
suggested_validation: Perform ATAC-seq on sorted high-feature-activation megakaryocyte precursors vs low-activation controls to confirm global chromatin accessibility increase, paired with seahorse metabolic flux analysis to validate glycolytic dependence and lactate production.

programme_name: Nuclear-cytoplasmic transport and RNA processing
functional_description: This programme coordinates active nuclear import/export machinery (RANBP1, HMGN2, HMGB1) with RNA-binding proteins (hnRNPs A1/A2B1/A3/C) to support rapid mRNA processing and nucleocytoplasmic trafficking in highly proliferative progenitors. The co-activation of mitochondrial phosphate transporters (SLC25A3, SLC25A5) and PPIase activity (PPIA) indicates simultaneous biosynthetic preparation of energy metabolism to support the transcription and translation demands of cell cycle progression.
key_evidence: RANBP1: Ran-GTPase complex regulates nuclear import of cell cycle regulators and ribosomal proteins during S/G2 phase
HMGB1 + HMGN2: Nucleosome remodeling factors facilitating open chromatin and transcription factory assembly in cycling cells
HNRNPA1/A2B1/A3/C: Coordinated mRNA splicing and export complex ensuring rapid processing of proliferation-associated transcripts
SLC25A3 + SLC25A5: Mitochondrial carriers supporting ATP and dNTP production for DNA replication and protein synthesis
PPIA: PPIase chaperone enabling proper folding of nuclear import machinery (importins) and ribosomal proteins
suggested_validation: Perform proximity ligation assay (PLA) between RANBP1 and importin-α/β in sorted Large Pre-B and Pro-Erythroblast cells, combined with qPCR quantification of nascent transcripts from hnRNP-dependent genes (e.g., cell cycle cyclins) after HNRNPA1 knockdown to directly test the coupling of nuclear import activity with cell-cycle-dependent transcription.

programme_name: Mitochondrial biogenesis and ribosome assembly
functional_description: This programme coordinates early erythroid progenitor expansion through simultaneous mitochondrial ATP synthesis capacity building and ribosomal protein production. The enrichment of ATP synthase components (ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1), iron storage machinery (FTH1), and extensive ribosomal proteins reflects the intense biosynthetic and energetic demands of basophilic erythroblasts undergoing rapid proliferation before haemoglobin synthesis dominates.
key_evidence: ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1: mitochondrial ATP synthase assembly—energy supply for proliferation
FTH1: iron storage capacity—preparing for massive haem synthesis ahead
RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0, RPS24, PA2G4: ribosomal protein enrichment—protein synthetic burst during G1/S
NOP10: snoRNP-mediated rRNA modification—ribosome maturation and assembly
YBX1, HMGB1: RNA-binding proteins facilitating ribosome biogenesis and nucleolar function
S100A6: calcium buffering—likely supporting metabolic transitions and cell cycle progression
suggested_validation: Combine mitochondrial mass quantification (TMRM or MitoTracker staining) with BrdU incorporation and rRNA synthesis assays (pulse-chase with 3H-uridine) in sorted pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts to confirm coordinated mitochondrial biogenesis with S-phase entry and ribosomal output.

programme_name: Ubiquitin-proteasome protein quality control
functional_description: Active protein degradation and turnover programme essential during erythroid and megakaryocytic proliferation, coordinating proteasomal protein clearance (UBB, RBX1) with translational stress response (EIF2AK1) and nucleotide excision repair (RAD23A). This programme maintains proteostasis during the massive biosynthetic demands of terminal differentiation and polyploidisation.
key_evidence: UBB: core ubiquitin conjugation substrate for proteasomal degradation pathways
RBX1: essential RING-finger component of E3 ubiquitin ligase complexes
EIF2AK1: translational attenuation kinase responding to heme/amino acid stress in erythropoiesis
RAD23A: nucleotide excision repair adaptor indicating DNA damage surveillance during replication
YBX1: mRNA stability/translation modulation under stress conditions
suggested_validation: Proteasome activity assay (e.g., chymotrypsin-like substrate cleavage) in sorted polychromatic erythroblasts vs. non-erythroid controls, combined with polyubiquitin immunofluorescence to visualize active protein degradation flux.

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and translational capacity
functional_description: This programme coordinates ribosomal protein synthesis and assembly machinery, alongside translation initiation/elongation factors, to rapidly expand translational capacity in proliferating progenitors. The enrichment of both 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0) combined with translation factors (EEF1B2) indicates active ribosome production and assembly rather than active translation per se. The concurrent upregulation of chaperones (PPIA) and antioxidant enzymes (GSTP1, MT-CO2) suggests coordinated management of proteotoxic stress during high-rate protein synthesis.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0: six distinct ribosomal protein components indicating concerted ribosome assembly across both subunits
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor GEF activity required to sustain high translation rates once ribosomes are assembled
PPIA: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase chaperone function critical for nascent protein folding during rapid synthesis burst
GSTP1, MT-CO2: detoxification and mitochondrial respiration capacity to fuel and manage byproducts of translational acceleration
HMGN2: chromatin remodeling protein supporting transcriptionally active chromatin state for ribosomal and translation factor genes
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling (sucrose gradient fractionation) on sorted Megakaryocyte Precursors and Large Pre-B cells with high vs low SAE feature activation to quantify free ribosomal subunits, monosomes, and actively translating polysome populations.

programme_name: Ribosomal biogenesis and mitochondrial ATP coupling
functional_description: This programme represents coordinated upregulation of ribosomal protein components (RPL4, RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS2) coupled with mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation machinery (ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1, NME4) and nucleolar assembly factors (NOP10, PA2G4). This specific co-activation reflects the bioenergetic demands of early erythroblasts undergoing rapid protein synthesis for haemoglobin production, with matched ATP generation capacity and ribosome assembly to sustain biosynthetic flux.
key_evidence: RPL4, RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS2: direct ribosomal structural components required for translation of haemoglobin and other biosynthetic proteins
ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1, NME4: mitochondrial ATP synthase and nucleotide kinase coupling oxidative capacity to biosynthetic demand
NOP10, PA2G4: nucleolar snoRNP assembly and pre-ribosomal processing essential for ribosome biogenesis during proliferation
FTH1, S100A6: iron storage and calcium signalling supporting haem synthesis and metabolic coordination in erythroblast differentiation
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling on sorted basophilic/pro-erythroblasts with and without selective ATP synthase inhibition (oligomycin); feature activation should correlate with active translation rate and collapse upon bioenergetic stress, demonstrating mechanistic linkage between oxidative capacity and ribosomal function.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and oxidative metabolism
functional_description: This feature captures coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits) combined with mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation machinery and protein folding chaperones. This represents the energetically demanding biosynthetic phase of erythro-megakaryocytic differentiation, where rapidly proliferating progenitors must simultaneously synthesize massive amounts of cytoplasmic protein (haemoglobin in erythroblasts; platelet-specific proteins in megakaryocytes) while meeting ATP demands through oxidative metabolism.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPS26, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4: Core 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components essential for translation capacity in high-protein-synthesis cells
MT-CO2, UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components indicating elevated oxidative phosphorylation to fuel ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis
PPIA, TXN: Protein folding chaperones (peptidyl-prolyl isomerase and thioredoxin) managing proteostasis under high protein synthesis load
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting sustained translation elongation rates
HNRNPA1, SNRPE: RNA metabolism factors supporting mRNA processing and ribosomal RNA biogenesis
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling on sorted CFU-E and Megakaryocyte Precursor cells compared to quiescent HSPCs to quantify translation capacity; correlate polysome abundance with SAE feature activation strength and validate mitochondrial oxygen consumption rates (Seahorse assay) in feature-high vs feature-low populations.

programme_name: Pre-BCR signalling and S-phase burst
functional_description: Coordinated programme supporting active DNA replication and cell cycle progression in large pre-B cells. Combines dNTP synthesis (TYMS), microtubule dynamics (STMN1, TUBA1B, TUBB), chromatin remodelling (HMGB1/2, HMGN2, H2AFZ), and anti-apoptotic signalling (PTMA) to sustain proliferation.
key_evidence: TYMS: rate-limiting dNTP synthesis enzyme required for DNA replication
STMN1: destabilizes microtubules; essential for mitotic spindle dynamics in G2/M
TUBA1B & TUBB: core spindle apparatus structural proteins
HMGB1/2 & HMGN2: nucleosome remodelling and transcriptional activation during S-phase
PTMA: apoptosis suppression maintains cell viability during replication stress
suggested_validation: BrdU/EdU incorporation assay combined with flow cytometry to confirm S-phase enrichment in STMN1-high large pre-B cells; validate TYMS dependency with dTMP supplementation or TYMS inhibition experiments

programme_name: Mitochondrial biogenesis and ribosomal assembly
functional_description: This programme represents the coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation machinery (ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1, NME4) coupled with ribosomal protein synthesis capacity (RPLP0, RPL37A, PA2G4) and nucleolar activity (NOP10). This reflects the intense metabolic and translational demand of early erythro-megakaryocyte progenitors preparing for massive haemoglobin and megakaryocyte protein synthesis during terminal differentiation.
key_evidence: ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1, NME4: Mitochondrial ATP synthesis and energy metabolism upregulation required for high-rate protein synthesis
RPLP0, RPL37A, PA2G4: Ribosomal assembly and rRNA processing for rapid translation capacity expansion
NOP10: snoRNP component essential for rRNA modification and ribosome biogenesis
FTH1: Iron storage capacity expansion coordinated with increased haem synthesis for erythroid differentiation
YBX1, SRSF3: RNA binding and splicing factors supporting translational and transcriptional remodelling
suggested_validation: Quantify mitochondrial mass by MitoTracker staining and correlate with ribosomal activity (e.g., puromycin incorporation assay or polysome profiling) in sorted Pro-Erythroblasts and Basophilic Erythroblasts expressing high vs low Feature 850 activity.

programme_name: Erythro-megakaryocytic proliferation and RNA metabolism
functional_description: A coordinated gene expression programme supporting rapid proliferation in erythroid and megakaryocytic progenitors through enhanced mitochondrial energy production, iron storage, and replication-associated RNA processing. The programme balances metabolic demands of high cell division rates with biosynthetic capacity for ribosomal RNA and histone-mRNA coordination.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage essential for haem synthesis during massive red cell production
SLBP: Replication-dependent histone mRNA binding required for S-phase progression in proliferating progenitors
ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1: Mitochondrial ATP synthase components supporting energy demands of erythro-megakaryocytic expansion
NOP10: snoRNP component involved in ribosomal RNA modification and biogenesis during rapid growth
YBX1, HNRNPF, PA2G4: RNA-binding proteins regulating growth-associated mRNA processing and stability
suggested_validation: Flow cytometric assessment of mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM staining) and BrdU incorporation in sorted erythroblast/megakaryocyte progenitors to confirm proliferative state and energy metabolism elevation

programme_name: Mitochondrial bioenergetics and translational capacity
functional_description: This feature represents coordinated upregulation of oxidative phosphorylation machinery (COX5A, VDAC1, SLC25A3/A5), ribosomal proteins (RPS2/23/24, RPL4), and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2, PPIA) in metabolically demanding precursor cells. The programme couples mitochondrial ATP generation with enhanced protein synthesis capacity, indicating active biosynthetic commitment in megakaryocyte and dendritic cell precursors preparing for rapid proliferation and maturation.
key_evidence: COX5A, VDAC1, SLC25A3/A5: terminal electron transport chain and mitochondrial substrate transport—direct markers of oxidative ATP production
RPS2/23/24, RPL4, EEF1B2: coordinated ribosomal and translation machinery—signature of high translation flux matching energy availability
GSTP1, PTMA, YBX1: stress-response chaperones and nucleic acid binding proteins—enable proteostasis under high protein synthesis load
ENO1: glycolytic enzyme supporting Pasteur effect and biosynthetic precursor synthesis in proliferating precursors
suggested_validation: Metabolic profiling (Seahorse XFe) on sorted high-feature-activation megakaryocyte precursors vs background cells to confirm elevated OXPHOS and glycolysis rates; correlate with nascent protein synthesis rates (puromycin incorporation) to validate translation coupling.

programme_name: mRNA splicing and ribosome assembly
functional_description: Active coordination of pre-mRNA processing and ribosomal protein synthesis in rapidly proliferating progenitors. The feature captures concurrent upregulation of splicing machinery (SRSF2/3, HNRNPs) and ribosomal structural proteins, reflecting the biosynthetic demand of megakaryocyte and pre-B cell expansion during active differentiation.
key_evidence: SRSF3, SRSF2: SR-protein splicing factors essential for constitutive and alternative splicing in proliferating cells
HNRNPC, HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1, HNRNPR: hnRNP complex members regulating pre-mRNA processing and spliceosome function
RPS24, RPLP0: ribosomal structural proteins indicating coordinated ribosome assembly to support translation demands
HMGN2, HMGB1: chromatin-associated proteins facilitating access to actively transcribed genes during proliferation
PTMA: apoptosis suppressor maintaining cell viability during rapid division
suggested_validation: Perform RNA-seq with polysome profiling or ribosome sequencing on sorted Megakaryocyte Precursors vs mature megakaryocytes to confirm co-activation of splicing and translation machinery specifically during the expansion phase, distinguishing this from mature terminal differentiation programmes.
prior_programme_name: Progenitor cell proliferation and RNA processing

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and mRNA processing
functional_description: This programme coordinates ribosomal protein synthesis and mRNA splicing machinery assembly, essential for rapidly proliferating progenitors undergoing massive protein synthesis during differentiation. The co-expression of 40S/60S ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0) with SR-rich splicing factors (SRSF2, SRSF3) and RNA-binding proteins (YBX1, HNRNPC) reflects the coupling of ribosome biogenesis with pre-mRNA processing — a hallmark of cells preparing for translational capacity expansion.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0: Direct ribosomal protein components of 40S/60S subunits required for ribosome assembly in proliferating cells
SRSF2, SRSF3: SR-family splicing factors that regulate alternative splicing of proliferation-associated transcripts and ribosomal protein mRNAs
YBX1, HNRNPC: RNA-binding proteins that facilitate mRNA stability and ribosome occupancy during high-throughput translation
SLC25A3: Mitochondrial phosphate transporter supporting ATP synthesis for energetically-expensive ribosome biogenesis
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase accelerating ribosomal protein folding during assembly
suggested_validation: Perform ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) on sorted Megakaryocyte Precursors and Pro-Erythroblasts with high vs low SAE feature activation to quantify global translation rates and ribosome footprint density, coupled with quantitative mass spectrometry of nascent ribosomal subunit assembly complexes.

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and mitochondrial OXPHOS
functional_description: This feature captures a coordinated biosynthetic programme in early-stage erythroblasts characterized by simultaneous upregulation of ribosomal protein components (RPLP0, RPS17, RPS23) and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (Complex I and III subunits: NDUFS5, UQCRH, UQCRQ). This reflects the intense metabolic demand of haemoglobin synthesis, which requires both translational capacity and ATP generation through oxidative metabolism to support massive protein production during erythroid proliferation.
key_evidence: RPLP0/RPS17/RPS23: Direct structural components of ribosomes required for the extraordinary translational burden of haemoglobin synthesis in basophilic/polychromatic erythroblasts
NDUFS5/UQCRH/UQCRQ: Mitochondrial electron transport chain subunits indicating heightened oxidative phosphorylation to fuel ATP-intensive protein synthesis
PA2G4: RNA-binding protein in pre-ribosomal complexes, marking active ribosome biogenesis rather than just protein translation
SNRPG/SNRPD1/SNRPE: spliceosomal components indicating concurrent mRNA processing during high biosynthetic flux
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase facilitating protein folding during massive haemoglobin chain synthesis
suggested_validation: Perform mitochondrial stress tests (FCCP treatment) combined with ribosomal profiling in sorted basophilic erythroblasts to demonstrate coordinated collapse of both OXPHOS and polysome density, and quantify haemoglobin synthesis rate as functional output of this integrated programme.

programme_name: Mitochondrial bioenergetics and oxidative metabolism
functional_description: This feature captures a coordinated programme of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, glycolytic flux, and mitochondrial biogenesis specifically active in metabolically demanding progenitors. The enrichment of electron transport chain components (COX5A), ATP/ADP exchange machinery (SLC25A5), and glycolytic enzymes (ENO1, LDHA) alongside proteasomal components indicates cells sustaining high ATP turnover with rapid protein quality control—characteristic of megakaryocyte precursors and proliferating dendritic cell precursors undergoing active biomass accumulation.
key_evidence: COX5A, SLC25A5: terminal oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial ATP export for energy-demanding biosynthesis
LDHA, ENO1: glycolytic backup and lactate metabolism supporting rapid proliferation without full oxidative reliance
VDAC1, UCP2: mitochondrial outer membrane dynamics and uncoupling capacity enabling metabolic flexibility
PSMA4, RBX1: proteasomal and ubiquitin-dependent protein turnover supporting remodelling of metabolic machinery
GSTP1: antioxidant defence against ROS generated by high mitochondrial activity
suggested_validation: Perform Seahorse XF analysis (oxygen consumption rate vs extracellular acidification rate) on sorted megakaryocyte precursors and pre-cDC with high vs low SAE feature 1471 activation, combined with TMRM/JC-1 staining to quantify mitochondrial membrane potential dynamics.

programme_name: Proliferative chromatin accessibility and translation
functional_description: This feature captures the coordinated upregulation of chromatin remodeling proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1/2, H2AFZ/Y, H3F3A) that maintain open chromatin during active proliferation, coupled with enhanced protein synthesis machinery (ribosomal proteins, PPIA) and microtubule dynamics (STMN1, TUBB). The programme specifically marks the highly proliferative state of cycling B-cell precursors where transcriptional accessibility and translation capacity must be maintained at maximal levels to support rapid cell division.
key_evidence: HMGN2/HMGN1: nucleosomal proteins maintaining transcriptionally active chromatin architecture during S/G2 phase
HMGB1/HMGB2: non-histone DNA-binding proteins facilitating chromatin accessibility for replication and transcription
H3F3A/H2AFZ/H2AFY: histone variants incorporated during active replication to maintain chromatin plasticity
STMN1: microtubule destabilizer critical for mitotic spindle dynamics in fast-cycling cells
RPLP0/RPS24: ribosomal components enabling sustained protein synthesis during proliferation
PPIA: prolyl isomerase facilitating rapid protein folding during high translation rates
suggested_validation: ChIP-seq for H3K4me3 and H3K27ac combined with RNA-seq in sorted Pro-B Cycling vs Large Pre-B cells to validate that HMGN/HMGB proteins co-localize with active promoters specifically during the early cycling phase, and correlate STMN1 expression with mitotic index by immunofluorescence.

programme_name: Mitochondrial iron-sulfur biogenesis in early erythropoiesis
functional_description: This programme coordinates iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster assembly and mitochondrial energetics specifically in early erythroid progenitors during the high-proliferation phase. The coordinated upregulation of BOLA3 (Fe-S cluster synthesis), FTH1 (iron storage), and ATP synthase components (ATP5MC1, ATP5IF1) reflects the substantial metabolic demand of rapidly dividing erythroblasts that require both iron cofactors for cytochrome c oxidase assembly and robust ATP production. This represents a distinct metabolic programme separate from haemoglobin synthesis, reflecting the need to balance cellular proliferation with iron homeostasis.
key_evidence: BOLA3: essential Fe-S cluster biogenesis required for Complex III/IV assembly in high-energy proliferating cells
FTH1: iron storage capacity must expand to support Fe-S synthesis without toxic iron accumulation
ATP5MC1 + ATP5IF1: mitochondrial ATP synthase components indicating elevated OXPHOS demand during S/G2 phase proliferation
NOP10: H/ACA snoRNP component involved in ribosomal RNA pseudouridylation, supporting rapid ribosome biogenesis in proliferating progenitors
YBX1 + PA2G4: RNA-binding proteins coordinating ribosome assembly and translation efficiency during rapid biomass accumulation
suggested_validation: Perform BioID proximity labeling from BOLA3 in sorted Pro-Erythroblasts vs Basophilic Erythroblasts to map the Fe-S cluster synthesis interactome, coupled with quantitative Fe-S cluster content measurement and iron isotope tracing to confirm active Fe-S biogenesis specifically in high-BOLA3 cells.

programme_name: Mitotic spindle assembly and RNA processing
functional_description: This programme coordinates active cell cycle progression through mitosis specifically in megakaryocyte and erythroid precursors. The feature captures a distinct sub-programme combining spindle checkpoint machinery (ERH, TUBA1B, YWHAQ/E 14-3-3 proteins), SR-rich splicing factors (SRSF2/3), and nuclear organization proteins (HMGB1, DEK, RANBP1) that support rapid RNA processing during S/G2/M phases when both transcription and translation demands are high.
key_evidence: ERH: mitosis-specific factor localizing to midbody; direct marker of active cytokinesis
SRSF2/SRSF3: SR-rich splicing factors driving cell-cycle-regulated alternative splicing during proliferation
YWHAQ/YWHAE: 14-3-3 proteins mediating mitotic checkpoint signaling through phospho-serine binding
TUBA1B: tubulin component essential for spindle microtubule assembly during M phase
HMGB1/DEK: chromatin remodeling proteins facilitating transcription in proliferating cells with condensed chromatin
RANBP1: nuclear transport factor coordinating nucleocytoplasmic transport during mitosis when NPC permeability changes
suggested_validation: Live-cell imaging of sorted megakaryocyte precursors and polychromatic erythroblasts using FUCCI cell cycle reporter, combined with immunofluorescence for ERH/TUBA1B at different cell cycle phases to confirm feature activation specifically during S/G2/M transitions.

programme_name: Proliferative metabolic priming in megakaryocytes
functional_description: This feature captures a coordinated programme of glycolytic activation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and RNA processing that prepares megakaryocyte precursors for rapid proliferation. The enrichment of metabolic enzymes (GAPDH, ENO1, LDHA), mitochondrial carriers (VDAC1, SLC25A5), and splicing factors (SRSF3, HNRNPC) indicates active bioenergetic restructuring concurrent with increased transcriptional demand during megakaryocytic proliferation.
key_evidence: GAPDH, ENO1, LDHA: Glycolytic pathway enzymes enabling high ATP production without oxidative phosphorylation—hallmark of proliferating cell metabolism
VDAC1, SLC25A5: Mitochondrial outer membrane and ATP/ADP exchange proteins supporting energy substrate availability for cell division
SRSF3, HNRNPC, YBX1, ERH: RNA-binding and splicing factors mediating rapid mRNA processing and nucleocytoplasmic transport required for proliferation-scale protein synthesis
YWHAQ, HMGN2, HMGB1: Cell cycle signaling adaptors and chromatin-active proteins enabling coordinated gene expression during proliferative remodeling
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor stabilizing survival signals during the metabolically demanding proliferative phase
suggested_validation: Perform real-time metabolic profiling (Seahorse XF assay) comparing high vs low Feature 1760 activation in sorted megakaryocyte precursors to quantify glycolytic dependency, ATP production rate, and mitochondrial bioenergetic capacity; pair with single-cell RNA-seq velocity analysis to confirm this programme precedes rapid megakaryocytic polyploidization.

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and histone mRNA processing
functional_description: This feature captures a coordinated programme of ribosomal RNA processing, ribosome assembly, and replication-dependent histone mRNA metabolism specifically active in proliferating megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitors. The convergence of snoRNP components (NOP10), histone mRNA-specific machinery (SLBP), ribosomal proteins (RPLP0, MRPS34), and splicing factors indicates active preparation of translational capacity during rapid cell division and massive cytoplasmic expansion.
key_evidence: SLBP: stem-loop histone mRNA binding protein—essential for processing replication-dependent histone transcripts, only needed during active S-phase in megakaryocytes and erythroblasts undergoing DNA synthesis
NOP10: H/ACA snoRNP component—catalyses pseudouridylation of ribosomal RNA, rate-limiting for ribosome biogenesis in highly proliferative compartments
RPLP0, MRPS34: ribosomal protein subunits—direct markers of ongoing ribosome assembly to support massive haemoglobin/platelet protein synthesis demands
SRSF2, SRSF3, SNRPG: splicing machinery—coordinate pre-mRNA processing including histone pre-mRNA 3' end formation (SLBP-dependent)
HMGB1, YBX1: nucleic acid chaperones—facilitate ribosome assembly and histone mRNA structuring during replication stress
suggested_validation: RT-qPCR quantifying SLBP mRNA and histone H3/H4 mRNA ratios (characteristic stem-loop structure) in sorted G1 vs S-phase megakaryocyte precursors and basophilic erythroblasts; BrdU incorporation should correlate with feature activation to confirm S-phase specificity.

programme_name: RNA processing and proteostasis in proliferating progenitors
functional_description: This feature marks a coordinated programme of RNA splicing, ribosome biogenesis, and protein quality control specifically active in proliferating megakaryocyte and erythroid progenitors. The dominance of spliceosomal components (SRSF2, SRSF3, SNRPG, LSM5), RNA-binding proteins (YBX1, HNRNPA2B1, HMGB1), and proteostasis factors (UBB, RBX1, SOD1) suggests active management of RNA processing demands and oxidative stress during rapid cell division.
key_evidence: SRSF2/SRSF3: SR-rich splicing factors indicating high-throughput pre-mRNA processing requirements during proliferation
SNRPG/LSM5: spliceosomal U-snRNP components essential for sustained splicing capacity
YBX1: cold-shock domain RNA-binding protein stabilizing transcripts under replication stress
HNRNPA2B1: hnRNP family member coordinating alternative splicing during cell division
RBX1/UBB: ubiquitin-proteasome machinery for rapid protein turnover during progenitor expansion
SOD1: antioxidant defence maintaining redox homeostasis in metabolically active progenitors
IDH2: NADPH-generating enzyme supporting biosynthesis and antioxidant responses
suggested_validation: Perform RNA-seq on sorted high vs low feature-activation megakaryocyte precursors to validate splicing factor enrichment; follow with ribosome profiling to confirm elevated translation demand and use of specific isoforms during this differentiation stage.

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and mRNA processing
functional_description: This programme represents coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS24, RPS2), spliceosomal components (SNRPG, SNRPB, SRSF3), and histone mRNA-specific processing factors (SLBP) in erythro-megakaryocytic progenitors. The activation reflects intense translational capacity building and mRNA maturation required for rapid cytoplasmic expansion during differentiation, coupled with nuclear protein quality control (YBX1, HMGB1, RANBP1) to manage the transcriptional and translational surge.
key_evidence: RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS24, RPS2: Coordinated ribosomal protein expression enabling high-capacity protein synthesis in proliferating progenitors
SLBP: Histone mRNA stem-loop binding protein specifically required for replication-dependent histone synthesis during S-phase in erythroid/megakaryocytic expansion
SNRPG, SNRPB, SRSF3: Spliceosomal factors and SR-family splicing regulators supporting massive mRNA processing flux
YBX1, HMGB1: Cold shock domain and HMG-box proteins managing nucleic acid binding during high transcriptional/translational demand
RANBP1: Nuclear-cytoplasmic transport regulator coordinating import of ribosomal subunits and export of processed mRNAs
suggested_validation: Perform ribosome profiling ± polysome gradient analysis on sorted Basophilic/Polychromatic Erythroblasts vs CFU-E to quantify translation initiation rates and ribosomal occupancy, coupled with metabolic labelling (e.g. puromycin incorporation) to confirm spike in active protein synthesis in high-feature-activation cells.

programme_name: Erythroid stress response and proteostasis
functional_description: This programme activates in early erythroid progenitors (Pro-Erythroblasts and CFU-E) undergoing rapid proliferation and hemoglobin synthesis, characterized by coordinated upregulation of molecular chaperones, oxidative stress defences, and protein quality control mechanisms. The co-expression of heat shock proteins (DNAJA1), antioxidants (TXN, SOD1), ribosomal proteins, and nuclear organization factors (LMNA) reflects the metabolic demands and proteotoxic stress associated with massive globin chain synthesis.
key_evidence: DNAJA1: Hsp40 co-chaperone required for protein folding during high-rate hemoglobin synthesis
TXN & SOD1: Redox balance maintenance critical for iron metabolism and RBC maturation
LMNA: Nuclear lamina integrity during rapid cell division in early erythroid progenitors
RPL37A & RPS23: Ribosomal proteins reflecting translational demand for globin synthesis
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor enabling survival under proteotoxic and oxidative stress
CD63 & LEPROT: Endosomal/membrane trafficking supporting iron uptake and receptor recycling
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence of DNAJA1 + TXN with CD71 and hemoglobin staining in sorted Pro-Erythroblasts vs CFU-E to confirm proteostasis activation correlates with hemoglobin synthesis intensity; validate with proteasome/autophagy flux assays under iron replete vs depleted conditions
